# The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#value-semantics-layer)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-20**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.23629v1) · arXiv:2611.23629v1, submitted 17 November 2026.

**Reading coverage:** All 7 PDF pages: Sections 1–6, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–3 and captions, and references. Figures 1–3 and Table 2 were also visually inspected. No appendices or separately linked scientific supplement in this version.

## Research question

Schemas and ordinary descriptions may omit the operational meaning needed to translate analytical concepts into appropriate SQL.

## Method

VSL persists assertions about semantic roles, permissible operations, contextual conditions, supporting evidence and heuristic confidence. A Blue NL2SQL prototype supplies these assertions through prompting or planning plus a deterministic sqlglot-based checker and targeted regeneration.

## Evaluation

The authors select 124 non-policy operationalization failures from 236 intents across finance, public safety and HR. GPT-4o runs once per case. Author-assigned full/partial/unresolved labels compare two VSL variants, plain descriptions and information-matched prose.

## What the results support

Fully resolved cases rise from 20 with matched prose to 35 with VST prompting and 51 with planner integration. Process cases improve from 3/40 to 16/40, but quantitative cases fall from 11/20 to 8/20. Regeneration triggers on 6% of cases.

## Limits and qualifications

Selected failures and domain-specific intent patterns overlapping evaluation phrasing restrict generalization. Planning and regeneration effects are not isolated. Partial-credit grounding is not full-resolution accuracy. Assertion confidence is uncalibrated, the checker misses some invalid operations, and clarification, conflict alternatives, drift revalidation and compositional validity remain unimplemented or open. No VSL-specific release was verified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An adjacent test of operational context and bounded SQL validation, with clear remaining gaps between executable queries, admissible operations and the user's intended analytical proxy.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

Table 2 also reports a quantitative-category decline from 11 to 8 fully resolved cases. | Section 4, Results; Table 2, pp. 5–6 | Do not report 92.7% as full correctness or universal category improvement. Prefer the full-resolution counts and retain the regression. |
| The prototype detects conflicting meanings and asks users to clarify them. | The implementation-scope paragraph explicitly lists low-margin alternative retention and clarification, empirical confidence calibration and drift revalidation as unimplemented. Current consolidation thresholds to one interpretation. | Section 4, Implementation scope, p. 5; Section 5 C1, p. 6 | Treat these as research goals, not implemented ambiguity or abstention capabilities. |
| The comparison isolates reliable semantic enforcement independently of extra inference and prior information. | The information-matched prose control carries the same facts, but planner integration bundles planning constraints and regeneration. Author-assigned single-run labels, overlapping intent patterns and curated failure selection are explicit. The checker missed an unsupported filter and invalid progression comparison. | Section 4, Evaluation/Results/Overhead, pp. 5–6 | Evidence supports a bounded prototype comparison, not a causal estimate of enforcement alone, general semantic correctness, or end-to-end overhead of about 1 ms. |
